limitations: Static analysis only: the application was never installed, started, tested or exploited; no runtime verification of any finding was performed.

Timings were taken from the system clock: run started at 13:17:16 +08:00, the output files were written at 13:27-13:32 +08:00. The analysis phase stayed inside the 30-minute budget and the writing phase inside the 5-minute budget (total elapsed about 15 minutes).

Only the files inside the input directory and the rules in rules-v1 were used; no parent directories, external repositories, advisories, network access, standard answers or scoring code were consulted.

Coverage is uneven: all Python sources of the three applications were read in full, but most HTML templates, static CSS/JS assets, migrations and shell scripts were only inspected through targeted searches (|safe / mark_safe / csrf_token / innerHTML / eval / subprocess / raw()), so template-level issues that do not involve those patterns may have been missed.

Several findings (for example finding-046 and finding-047) depend on runtime behaviour such as module re-import or library sandbox details; they are marked with reduced confidence and list the unverified condition in metadata.preconditions.

Deployment-specific facts (reachable routes, proxy configuration, installed dependency versions, database contents) could not be checked and are recorded per finding as 'needs deployment confirmation'.

input_tokens / output_tokens / cost are null because no token accounting was available to the agent; the operator should fill them from the pi run log (session id 01a1e7ef-1c38-71b0-90d9-a1661beaf8c3).
notes: confirmed_model_id / pi_version / reasoning_effort were read from the runtime environment (PI_MODEL=MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, PI_PROVIDER=minimax-cn, PI_REASONING_LEVEL=high, `pi --version` -> 1.5.0). They describe the process that produced this run, not an independent verification of model identity.
